title: Bill 17 motion deferred; veterans crosswalk approved
subtitle: Creek expropriation, two rezonings, parking restrictions, utility write-offs and a recognition of long-serving staff.
overview: Council put off a decision on a motion urging the Province to review Bill 17, which changes how municipalities handle development applications and development charges. After hearing four delegates in support, Council deferred the motion to a special meeting on October 6 {{vote:m1}}, so members can settle on the preferred advocacy approach.

Council directed staff to work with the Royal Canadian Legion to install a veterans-themed commemorative crosswalk, aiming for Remembrance Day 2025 or, more realistically according to staff, 2026 {{vote:m9}}. It also approved the expropriation of 150-160 Borden Avenue South for the Schneider and Shoemaker Creeks Naturalization Project {{vote:m11}}, after an in-camera discussion.

Council also approved two zoning changes, new parking and stopping restrictions on several streets, and the write-off of uncollectable utility accounts. Earlier in the evening, Council recognized three employees for 20 years of service and heard an impact report from Reep Green Solutions.

decisions.detail: Council deferred the motion urging the Province to review Bill 17 to the October 6, 2025 special meeting, to allow more time to confirm the advocacy approach {{vote:m1}}.
Staff are directed to work with the Royal Canadian Legion and community partners to install a veterans-themed crosswalk, with Remembrance Day 2025 or 2026 as the target {{vote:m9}}.
Council approved expropriating 150-160 Borden Avenue South for the Schneider and Shoemaker Creeks Naturalization Project and authorized the related legal steps {{vote:m11}}.
Council approved rezoning 157 Schweitzer Street from Residential Three (R-3) to Low Rise Residential Four (RES-4) with a site-specific provision {{vote:m7}}.
Council approved a site-specific provision for the Existing Use Floodplain Zone at 434-436 Queen Street South {{vote:m8}}.
Parking or weekday stopping is prohibited on sections of nine streets, including Otterbein Road, Karn Street and Madison Avenue South, and the Uniform Traffic By-law is amended {{vote:m4}}.
Council wrote off $121,784 in uncollectable utility accounts against the allowance for doubtful receivables {{vote:m5}}.

debate: Delegates supporting the Bill 17 motion argued that the bill weakens local ability to screen applications, set energy-efficiency and climate-resilience standards, and keep planning decisions with municipal staff rather than private consultants. One delegate raised concerns about province-wide setback reductions.

A delegate and one councillor raised the financial effect of collecting development charges later, at occupancy rather than at building permit. Several councillors said the funding gap was not addressed in the motion.

Some councillors said they would prefer advocacy that aligns more closely with the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and offers constructive suggestions. One example was letting staff approve small setback reductions instead of sending them to the Committee of Adjustment, which staff said they would support.
The Mayor suggested removing the last preamble clause and adding a clause on financial impacts so municipalities stay whole. Council then chose deferral to allow wording to be refined.
On the crosswalk, councillors spoke in support and noted its value for youth and for slowing traffic. Staff said a 2025 installation was unlikely and 2026 was most realistic.
